This is issue 4341: a struct declares a user-defined subscript operator and the
shader tries to write through it. The single line under test is the assignment
to the subscript, near the bottom of the entry point.

What to look for, pane by pane:

- The two DXC panes both fail, and the failure is on that one assignment line.
  Nothing else in the shader is rejected: reading through the same operator
  compiles, and so does a plain named mutating member function. The compiler
  cannot accept the write because HLSL has no way to declare an overload that
  returns something assignable.
- The last pane is the control. It compiles the identical source with the
  assignment removed by -DCONTROL_NO_ASSIGN, so a diagnostic in the earlier
  panes is attributable to that line and not to the struct, the profile or the
  compiler's HLSL support.

Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and its oldest DXC is 1.6.2112, which is
also the first release that accepts HLSL 2021 at all; the release history was
measured locally rather than here.
